costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an N47D20C typically takes 10-14 hours at £650-£910 total labour [EM-QUOTE] - the rear-mounted timing chain means engine-out access, which is why labour on this unit runs higher than front-chain designs. Confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.

failures.title: BMW N47D20C Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Failure
items.whatHappens: The N47's timing chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, against the gearbox. As the chain stretches and the tensioner wears, the first symptom is a metallic rattle on cold start; left unaddressed, the chain can jump or snap, putting valves into pistons and destroying the engine. Because the chain sits at the back, even a preventative replacement means removing the engine or gearbox - chain replacement alone runs £650-£1,800, and a full engine after catastrophic failure runs £2,500-£6,500 [EM-QUOTE].
items.repairVsReplace: Caught early - rattle only, no metal in the oil - a chain kit is the right call and far cheaper than a unit. Once the chain has jumped or let go, internal damage almost always means a replacement engine is the economical route; piecemeal head-and-piston repair on this engine rarely beats a rebuilt unit on price.

items.title: EGR Valve & Cooler Carbon Build-Up
items.onset: 80,000+ miles, earlier on short-trip cars [PATTERN DATA]
items.whatHappens: Like most Euro 5 diesels of its era, the N47D20C's EGR system carbons up, causing rough running, limp mode and - where the cooler leaks - coolant loss into the intake. It's a repair-level issue rather than an engine-killer, but on a car already facing chain work it often tips the maths toward a fully reconditioned unit with the EGR system addressed at the same time.
items.repairVsReplace: On its own, an EGR clean or replacement is a sensible standalone repair. It becomes a replacement argument only in combination with chain wear or turbo trouble.

items.title: Turbocharger Wear
items.whatHappens: Bearing wear and actuator faults show as whistle, smoke or lost boost. Not unusually frequent for the class, but worth checking on any used donor engine - a tired turbo on a used unit erodes the price advantage quickly.
items.repairVsReplace: A turbo alone is a repair. On a used replacement engine, insist on evidence the turbo was inspected.

failures.goodYearsLine: BMW revised the chain components during the N47's life, and the later B47 relocated the chain to the front of the engine entirely - but no N47D20C production year is considered free of the chain risk; specialist consensus is to treat chain history, not model year, as the deciding factor on this engine [PATTERN DATA].

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the N47D20C
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on the block - on the N47 it sits on the front face of the crankcase below the cylinder head - and appears in your service records; your V5C lists engine capacity but not the code itself, so a registration lookup or VIN check is the reliable route. Enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact unit before any quote goes out.

relatives.description: 2007-2010 - the original version, fitted to earlier 118d/318d/520d models. Not a straight swap: fuel injection components and electronic controls differ, and a swap typically needs loom, mount and ECU work. Early N47D20C blocks up to roughly 2011 share near-identical castings with the A and have been used as replacements for it, while later C blocks have different water pump and oil filter housing openings.
The 204hp+ twin-turbo high-output version (123d/125d/x25d). Different turbo hardware and internals; never interchangeable with the C despite the near-identical name.
2014 onward - the successor, not a variant. Front-mounted chain, different architecture; it does not retrofit into an N47 car.

variants.closing: If a supplier quotes you an "N47" without the full suffix, ask for it - the suffix is the difference between a bolt-in replacement and an expensive mismatch.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement N47D20C - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used N47D20C from £1,800 [EM-QUOTE] only makes sense with documented timing chain history - on this engine specifically, an undocumented used unit is a gamble on the exact component that killed the one you're replacing. It suits lower-value hosts where a reconditioned unit would exceed the car's worth.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The sweet spot for most N47D20C buyers. A proper recon addresses the chain, guides, tensioner and - done well - the EGR cooler in the same build, which is precisely the failure set from Section 5. At £3,200-£5,500 [EM-QUOTE] with a 12-24 month warranty, it removes the engine's defining risk rather than inheriting it.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: Justified where the host car is worth keeping long-term. A full rebuild at £4,500-£6,500 [EM-QUOTE] should include the complete chain kit with revised tensioner, injector attention, and a turbo inspection as standard; ask any quote to itemise those three.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Every option is available supply-only or fully fitted through our vetted UK network, with a minimum 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery - see supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Be honest about the host before committing. Typical N47D20C hosts span roughly £1,500 for an early E87 to £14,000 for a late F30 [EM-VERIFIED]. On E87, E90, E60 and E83 cars - most now worth under £4,000-£5,000 - a reconditioned unit at £3,200+ frequently approaches or exceeds the car's value, and evaluating scrap or a used unit first is the honest advice. F20, F30, F10 and F25 hosts generally still justify reconditioned or rebuilt spend.

related.title: Engines Related to the BMW N47D20C

items.description: The original 2007-2010 version with the highest documented chain failure rate of the whole family; if your car is a pre-2010 118d/318d/520d, that page is the one you need.
The 2014-onward replacement that moved the timing chain to the front of the engine, largely resolving the N47's defining weakness; owners of 2015+ diesels are usually on a B47 without realising it.
The twin-turbo high-output version fitted to the 123d, 125d and x25d models; different turbo hardware, different price bracket, not interchangeable with the C.
The 1.6-litre version fitted to the 114d and entry 116d; if your 116d is a 2012-on 1.6, your engine is on that page, not this one.
The six-cylinder 3.0d from the same era (330d/530d), sharing the rear-chain design and its access costs; relevant if you're weighing a 520d against a 530d purchase.
